newsitem.title: USA: Calif. bankruptcy filings rise sharply - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. bankruptcy filings rise sharply - report.

text.p: Bankruptcy filings in California rose sharply this year and are almost back up to the recession levels of four years ago, according to a report released Wednesday.
A total of 13,331 people and businesses filed for bankruptcy in July, up 7.3 percent from 12,409 the month before, and up 24.9 percent from 10,656 for July a year ago, CDB Infotek said.
The total for the first seven months of this year was 86,726, up 20 percent from 72,250 for 1995. This year's year-to-date total is the highest since 1992.

"The current increase is part of a nationwide trend that has surprised most economists. A rise in bankruptcies like this doesn't normally happen when the economy is growing," said Rick Rozar, CDB president.

"One reason for the increase might be that debt levels got out of hand in recent years because of easy credit availability. Another reason could be that people have become desensitized to what used to be a fairly traumatic event. They're now thinking about it in financial situations where it wouldn't have been considered a few years ago," he said.
CDB Infotek provides on-line access to public records nationwide.
